design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks for one thing, to close her FlexLine to new draws and keep paying monthly. The monthly payment line_ext_close_to_draws_payment records is fixed only after three things the records call for on a line 28 days past due: the late fee for the unpaid 2026-09-18 minimum, the credit-limit review of a line fifteen or more days past due, and the workout relief due on one late fee when a past-due line is closed. Each computation's factors all move its result on this world (6, 5, 4 and 5 factors), two read the borrower's personal loan, and the relief must follow the late fee.

SCOPE. This task claims line_ext_late_fee, line_ext_workout_fee_relief, line_ext_limit_review, line_ext_close_to_draws_payment with tools assess_late_fee_ba469c06, grant_workout_fee_relief_903cc630, apply_limit_review_5d0a2d8e, close_line_to_draws_7539d675; task 1 claims line_ext_returned_payment_fee, line_ext_backbilled_draw_fee, line_ext_returned_fee_relief, line_ext_limit_increase. The scopes are disjoint and cover all eight extended policies.

DEPENDENCY CHAIN. Surface goal (close to new draws) -> line_evt_draw_period_and_closure plus line_ext_close_to_draws_payment (the repayment payment, declared by two scoped overwrites to replace, only for a line the borrower closes, the base level-payment sentences together with the tier's repayment payment method and the closing record's level repayment-period payment) -> term, method and late-history cut read the balance, the limit and the late-fee count -> the late fee (+balance, +1 late fee), the review (-limit) and the relief (-balance) must be on the records first -> the relief's way of figuring reads the late fees of 12 months, so it waits on the late fee.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root line_ext_close_to_draws_payment (owner user, tool close_line_to_draws_7539d675). Prerequisites: line_ext_late_fee (assess_late_fee_ba469c06, agent), line_ext_workout_fee_relief (grant_workout_fee_relief_903cc630, agent), line_ext_limit_review (apply_limit_review_5d0a2d8e, agent).
Edge line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_late_fee: kind value_input, gate late_term_cut, form state; policy_source "Before the repayment payment is worked out, every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period must carry its late-fee entry."; condition "For the due date in next_due_date, whose minimum payment is still unpaid (amount_past_due above 0.00) more than late_fee_grace_days days later, a line_late_fee_assessed entry with that installment_due_date exists and outstanding_balance includes it."; false at the opening because next_due_date 2026-09-18 has 34.98 still unpaid 28 days later (more than the 10-day grace) and no line_late_fee_assessed entry names installment_due_date 2026-09-18. (initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.next_due_date = 2026-09-18; initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.amount_past_due = 34.98); resolved by assess_late_fee_ba469c06: Step 9 books the late fee (5.38) for 2026-09-18; the late-fee entries in 12 months become 2, the late-history cut moves from 3 to 6 months, and the balance rises by the fee.
Edge line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_limit_review: kind value_input, gate payment_method_code, form state; policy_source "The repayment payment is fixed only after a line fifteen or more days past due carries a credit-limit review decided on or after its oldest unpaid due date."; condition "When amount_past_due is above 0.00 and the closing date is fifteen or more days after next_due_date, a line_limit_requests entry with request_type decrease and decision_status approved has a decision_date on or after next_due_date, and credit_limit equals its approved_limit."; false at the opening because The line is 28 days past due (15 or more) and the line has no line_limit_requests entry at all, so no review decided on or after 2026-09-18 exists. (initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.amount_past_due = 34.98; initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.credit_limit = 4000.0); resolved by apply_limit_review_5d0a2d8e: Step 13 records the review and sets credit_limit to 3,300.00; the balance is then more than 75 percent of the limit and the payment method moves to the equal-share tier.
Edge line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_workout_fee_relief: kind value_input, gate conversion_balance, form state; policy_source "The repayment payment of a past-due line is not fixed until the line carries a courtesy fee-waiver entry against one of its late fees dated on or after its oldest unpaid due date."; condition "When amount_past_due is above 0.00, a line_fee_waived entry with waiver_reason courtesy, txn_date on or after next_due_date and a line_late_fee_assessed entry as its related entry is on the line, and outstanding_balance reflects it."; false at the opening because The line is past due and no line_fee_waived entry is dated on or after 2026-09-18 (the only courtesy waiver is dated 2025-09-20). (initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.amount_past_due = 34.98; initial_state.line_transactions.0e96a3af-a3cd-411b-82db-836775219523.txn_date = 2025-09-20); resolved by grant_workout_fee_relief_903cc630: Step 11 books the workout relief (10.12); conversion_balance falls by it.
Edge line_ext_workout_fee_relief -> line_ext_late_fee: kind value_input, gate relief_way, form state; policy_source "Workout relief is fixed only after every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period carries its late-fee entry."; condition "For the due date in next_due_date, whose minimum payment is still unpaid more than late_fee_grace_days days later, a line_late_fee_assessed entry with that installment_due_date exists."; false at the opening because For next_due_date 2026-09-18, unpaid past the grace, no line_late_fee_assessed entry with that installment_due_date exists. (initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.next_due_date = 2026-09-18; initial_state.credit_lines.7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817.amount_past_due = 34.98); resolved by assess_late_fee_ba469c06: Step 9 books that late fee; two late fees then stand in the last 12 months, so the relief is figured as the fee less 5.00 instead of the whole fee.
Topological order: line_ext_late_fee -> line_ext_workout_fee_relief -> line_ext_limit_review -> line_ext_close_to_draws_payment. Parallel edges: Edges: root <- late fee, root <- limit review, root <- workout relief, workout relief <- late fee. The relief must follow the late fee, as its own prerequisite sentence says: "Workout relief is fixed only after every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period carries its late-fee entry." The limit review commutes with both: it reads the limit, the days past due, returns, the loan and the line age, and its only balance read is the floor (outstanding balance rounded up to 100.00), which stays far below the result whatever the order; the late fee and the relief read nothing the review writes. Every admissible order was replayed: late_fee -> workout_fee_relief -> limit_review: late_fee 5.38, workout_fee_relief 10.12, limit_review 3,300.00, close_to_draws_payment 149.99; terminal limit 3,300.00, balance 2,592.27, minimum due 149.99 | late_fee -> limit_review -> workout_fee_relief: late_fee 5.38, limit_review 3,300.00, workout_fee_relief 10.12, close_to_draws_payment 149.99; terminal limit 3,300.00, balance 2,592.27, minimum due 149.99 | limit_review -> late_fee -> workout_fee_relief: limit_review 3,300.00, late_fee 5.38, workout_fee_relief 10.12, close_to_draws_payment 149.99; terminal limit 3,300.00, balance 2,592.27, minimum due 149.99. All three leave the same scored arguments and the same terminal state.
Deletion sensitivity: line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_late_fee: Skipping the late fee leaves one late-fee entry in 12 months (a 3-month cut instead of 6), the balance without the fee and a larger relief; the repayment payment becomes 139.96 instead of 149.99. | line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_limit_review: Skipping the review leaves the limit at 4,000.00, the balance under 75 percent of it, so the level payment applies; the repayment payment becomes 126.49 instead of 149.99. | line_ext_close_to_draws_payment -> line_ext_workout_fee_relief: Skipping the workout relief leaves conversion_balance 2,602.39; the repayment payment becomes 150.58 instead of 149.99. | line_ext_workout_fee_relief -> line_ext_late_fee: Skipping the late fee leaves one late fee in 12 months and 34.98 past due, above the 25.00 fee, so the relief is figured on the whole fee: 12.66 instead of 10.12.
No user hint: user_scenario raises only closing the line to new draws while paying down the balance; it names no late fee, no review, no limit, no waiver and no relief, and gives no hint that anything must be sorted first. The only reference to corrections is a passive reaction ('If the representative tells you that something on the line has to be booked, reviewed or adjusted before the closing can go through, you say they can go ahead') triggered by the agent's own explanation; her remark about last month's payment is a reaction only when the agent brings it up.
Tools do not block: task_tools.py: close_line_to_draws_7539d675 only updates status, draw_period_end_date and minimum_payment_due; assess_late_fee_ba469c06 creates one ledger entry and raises outstanding_balance; grant_workout_fee_relief_903cc630 creates one waiver entry and lowers it; apply_limit_review_5d0a2d8e creates one line_limit_requests row and updates credit_limit. None reads another entry, checks a status, a balance or a prior write, or returns an error; each writes faithfully whether or not any prerequisite is resolved.

FOUR-POINT TEST OF EACH PREREQUISITE SENTENCE (own-rule sentence, ordering connective, record-visible state, one write of this difficulty brings it about). C <- LF: "Before the repayment payment is worked out, every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period must carry its late-fee entry." - in the closing rule, "Before", a late-fee entry naming the due date, only assess_late_fee_ba469c06 books it. C <- LR: "The repayment payment is fixed only after a line fifteen or more days past due carries a credit-limit review decided on or after its oldest unpaid due date." - "only after", a decided decrease row dated on or after next_due_date, only apply_limit_review_5d0a2d8e records it. C <- WO: "The repayment payment of a past-due line is not fixed until the line carries a courtesy fee-waiver entry against one of its late fees dated on or after its oldest unpaid due date." - "not ... until", a courtesy waiver tied to a late fee and dated on or after next_due_date; of this difficulty's writes only grant_workout_fee_relief_903cc630 books one (the replacement relief books courtesy waivers against returned-payment fees only, and no request-based courtesy waiver is asked for). WO <- LF: "Workout relief is fixed only after every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period carries its late-fee entry." - only assess_late_fee_ba469c06 books a late-fee entry. All edges are state form; no action-form fallback. No status registration, persona line or tool order stands in for a real-world event: the missed due date, the partial payment, the returns and the loan late fee are seeded facts dated before the call.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. line_closed_to_draws: line_evt_draw_period_and_closure, only gate charge_off_threshold (charge-off) -> policy_scope; lifecycle active -> repayment by user, and the extended rule states that an active line past due but not frozen may be closed (Standard freezes at 30 days past due; the line is 28 days past due and active, so the closing is allowed - the frozen-line question of revision 1 cannot arise). line_late_fee_assessed: late_fee_grace (time; due date 2026-09-18, grace 10 days counted from the next day, exclusive; negative case 2026-09-28, positive from 2026-09-29; frozen_time 2026-10-16). line_fee_waived: once_per_fee on related_txn_id eb19cdef-7ca8-4e4e-893f-c385e67b7d3d (no waiver of it exists); courtesy_count and courtesy_window are restated by the overwrites (workout relief is granted without a request and is not bound by the request window; it is still granted only while fewer than 1 courtesy waiver is on the line in 12 months - the 2025-09-20 one is 13 months back). line_limit_changed: active_line (status active) and seasoning (time; 32 months on 2026-10-16; negative case 2024-07-21, boundary 2024-07-22 inclusive); a decrease never below the balance or the Standard minimum 2,500.00 (3,300.00 is above both).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target key credit_line_id 7ee835b4-423b-47ab-b842-bcc50f66e817. Ledger rows included: every line_transactions row of this line. Objects already settled: the 2025-07-18 and 2026-03-18 due dates carry late fees and were paid; both returns carry the fees the returned-payment fee paragraph figured on their booking dates (each was the line's most recent return then), the first relieved in full by the 2025-09-20 courtesy waiver; the two earlier late fees were booked only after their minimum payments had been paid in full past the grace period, so each is the flat late_fee_usd; every draw carries its 2.5 percent fee. The loan's 2026-09-05 late fee was paid 2026-09-22.

SEED ROLES. credit_lines row: tier, limit, APR 24.99, age 32 months, balance, minimum due, next due date 2026-09-18 with 34.98 past due. Partial payment 2026-09-25 (30.00): grace-payment share. Late fees 2025-08-01 and 2026-04-03: late-history share, the late-history cut, the relief's fee and its tie rule (both 25.00, the later one booked against), the relief's way of figuring. Returns 2025-09-12 and 2026-02-25: the review's return cut counts one in 12 months. Courtesy waiver 2025-09-20: prior-relief share (none in 12 months, one in 24). Draws: 7 in 12 months and 1,600.00 in 3 months (method tier, trim). Ledger total: the late fee's balance tier. Loan and loan ledger: the review's loan cut (loan late fee 2026-09-21), the affordability extension (largest installment 426.95, loan current).

PERSONA. Opening: wants the line closed to new draws, paying monthly. On request: mobile, date of birth, ZIP (SSN last four and email as extras); balance only roughly. Passive reactions: lets the agent book, review or adjust what is needed; cannot pay in full; no AutoPay; if the agent raises the late payment she says money has been tight; carries out the closing with the values read to her. Every action is reachable in one call.

DIFFICULTY. The agent must find three prerequisites the customer never mentions, the ordering between the late fee and the relief, the tie rule for the relief's fee, a lender review that lowers the limit and thereby changes the payment method, and apply 20 tiered factors, four of them methods that change the shape of the formula (min of the flat fee and 25 percent of the unpaid part against the larger of the two; the fee less a retained part against the amount past due against the whole fee; the kept-base cut against a doubled cut above 5,000.00 against the whole-limit cut; the equal-share payment against the larger of the level payment and the current-cycle minimum against the level payment).

STANDARD SOLUTION (executed replay, equal to gold). Steps 0-7 read; 8/9 late fee 5.38; 10/11 relief 10.12; 12/13 reviewed limit 3,300.00; 14/15 the customer closes with repayment_payment 149.99. FORWARD AND REVERSE REFERENCES. Rule -> compute_basis -> compute and back were swept by script for all eight policies: every compute_basis value is a verbatim rule fragment, every binding has a basis, every replaced_by and policy_source is a verbatim rule sentence, no factor binding reads another factor's binding, no factor id is a substring of a tool name (0 issues).

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GT. Gold actions cite next_due_date and amount_past_due, the 2026-04-03 and 2025-08-01 late fees, prior step 9, and the customer's opening line; the time gates cite frozen_time, next_due_date and open_date; seed_consistency checks every credit_lines and line_transactions row (draw fees recomputed at 2.5 percent with a 5.00 minimum; ledger sum equals the balance).

user_scenario:
You are Marisol Pereira, 45, the office manager of a dental practice in Phoenix. You have a Larkspur FlexLine line of credit and you have decided you are done drawing on it: you keep dipping into it for little things and you want it shut today so no more money can come out of it. You cannot pay the balance off right now and you are fine paying it down month by month; you just want the drawing to stop. You open by saying, in your own words, "I'd like to close my FlexLine to any more draws and just keep paying off what I owe." You speak plainly and a little tiredly, it has been a long week, and you would like this done in one call.

You give your details only as the representative asks for them, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 6025554319, your date of birth is 1981-04-09 (April 9, 1981), and your home ZIP code is 85016. If they need one more detail, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 4072, and your email is marisol.pereira@gmail.com. You do not know any account or reference numbers by heart, and you do not remember your balance to the cent; if asked, you say it is somewhere around two and a half thousand dollars and that they should go by what their system shows. If they bring up last month's payment, you say money has been tight and you paid what you could.

You do not know Larkspur's rules and you do not try to guess them. If the representative tells you that something on the line has to be booked, reviewed or adjusted before the closing can go through, you say they can go ahead and take care of it; you do not ask for the details of each entry and you do not bring up any charge yourself. If they ask whether you would rather pay the whole balance off today, you say you can't afford that right now. If they ask about AutoPay, you don't use it and you don't want to set it up today.

When the representative tells you what your monthly payment will be once the line is closed to draws, you accept it as long as they say it was worked out from your account; you never suggest a figure of your own and you do not haggle. Closing the line is your own decision, so when they hand you the step to close the line yourself, you carry it out with the line reference number and the monthly payment exactly as they read them to you, and then you read back what you see. Once you see the line shown as closed to new draws with that monthly payment, you thank them and end the call.
